help_adaptedTools.message: Some providers refuse oneOf, anyOf or allOf at the root of a tool schema. Explorer sent a plain object and stated the rule in the description; the page's own schema is unchanged.

help_annotationsBody.message: Annotations are claims declared by a tool, such as read-only or untrusted content. Explorer displays what the browser reports. They are not independent guarantees about what the tool does.

help_applyOverride.message: Save these changes for Explorer. A configured mock replaces the real tool call while active.

help_auditBody.message: Audit scores the contract each tool declares — description, schema, annotations — so a calling model can pick and call it correctly. It is quality of what a site published, not a safety verdict; the judgement of what to fix stays with you.

help_automateBody.message: Manual recipes reuse up to 20 reviewed calls without a model: named inputs and explicitly selected earlier result fields supply later arguments. Review the page, frames and local mocks, then run one step or the remaining steps. Pause and stop are explicit; interrupted runs never resume automatically. Agent Lab and Evals remain optional ways to test model-driven tool use; its Manual mode lets you drive the loop with a model of your own without Explorer sending anything.

Override changes Explorer’s local view and can simulate results; its active state is shown explicitly.

help_frameBody.message: An origin is the site address with its protocol and port. A frame is an embedded page. Two frames can expose tools with the same name; Explorer keeps their execution targets separate.

help_instrumentOff.message: Stop capturing new registration locations for this site. Reload the page to remove the instrumentation wrappers.

help_introBody.message: WebMCP lets a website expose named actions, called tools. Explorer shows those tools and lets you try them yourself. You do not need an AI account to inspect or run a tool.

help_introTitle.message: Explore what a website can do

help_manualReply.message: Parse the pasted model reply and continue the manual agent run. Tool calls in that reply may execute.

help_missingRegistrations.message: Inspect registrations seen by Instrumentation Mode that are absent from the browser’s exposed tools.

help_modelSetup.message: Choose a provider and model, manage its connection and set execution budgets.

help_nativeBody.message: Native means the browser provides the WebMCP API. A polyfill provides an implementation in JavaScript; the bundled demo uses one. A working demo does not prove that every website supports WebMCP.

help_nav_agent.message: Configure a model or manual mode, then give an agent a task using the page’s tools.

help_nav_audit.message: Score the quality of the tool contracts this page declares and export the findings.

help_nav_evals.message: Create repeatable tasks with expectations and compare agent runs.

help_nav_security.message: Passive findings from visible tool declarations, with evidence and sources. Indicators are not proven attacks. Review and fix generation invoke no tool. Origin scans and active probes require their own explicit actions below. Heuristic review of visible declarations, not a security certification. Unknown checks remain below. A high grade does not authorize an action.

sec_accepts_missing_required_fix.message: Check required arguments in the tool's code and return an error naming the missing one.
sec_accepts_missing_required_fix.description: Security finding accepts-missing-required: what to do.

sec_accepts_missing_required_title.message: The tool accepted a call without a required argument

sec_accepts_missing_required_why.message: Omitted a required property and the tool answered as if valid: the declared contract is not what the code enforces.
sec_accepts_missing_required_why.description: Security finding accepts-missing-required: why it matters.

sec_accepts_out_of_schema_input_fix.message: Validate every argument in the tool's code and return a descriptive error for a wrong type.
sec_accepts_out_of_schema_input_fix.description: Security finding accepts-out-of-schema-input: what to do.

sec_accepts_out_of_schema_input_title.message: The tool accepted an argument of the wrong type

sec_accepts_out_of_schema_input_why.message: Sent a value of another type than the schema declares and the tool answered as if valid. The browser does not validate arguments (measured, WMP-0046); the tool's code is the only validation layer (spec §6.3.1.3).
sec_accepts_out_of_schema_input_why.description: Security finding accepts-out-of-schema-input: why it matters.

sec_accepts_unbounded_input_fix.message: Bound the parameter with maxLength in the schema and enforce it in code.
sec_accepts_unbounded_input_fix.description: Security finding accepts-unbounded-input: what to do.

sec_accepts_unbounded_input_why.message: A free-text parameter without maxLength took a very long value. Length limits shrink the space an injected instruction can use (spec §6.4.2).
sec_accepts_unbounded_input_why.description: Security finding accepts-unbounded-input: why it matters.

sec_accepts_unknown_property_fix.message: Ignore or reject unknown properties deliberately, in code.
sec_accepts_unknown_property_fix.description: Security finding accepts-unknown-property: what to do.

sec_accepts_unknown_property_title.message: The tool accepted an unknown property

sec_accepts_unknown_property_why.message: An extra, undeclared property was accepted. Chrome's guidance allows loose schemas with strict code; this is a fact for the person who knows which it is.
sec_accepts_unknown_property_why.description: Security finding accepts-unknown-property: why it matters.

sec_consequential_without_hint_fix.message: Set annotations.consequentialHint to true, or rename the tool if it only starts a process the person completes.
sec_consequential_without_hint_fix.description: Security finding consequential-without-hint: what to do.

sec_consequential_without_hint_why.message: The name or description uses a verb that pays, sends, books, deletes or otherwise commits the person; without consequentialHint an agent may run it without asking (spec §6.4.5, §6.3.2).
sec_consequential_without_hint_why.description: Security finding consequential-without-hint: why it matters.

sec_convention_llms_txt_present_fix.message: Keep it accurate if you serve it; it is optional.
sec_convention_llms_txt_present_fix.description: Security finding convention-llms-txt-present: what to do.

sec_convention_llms_txt_present_why.message: llms.txt is an informal convention for a machine-readable site summary, checked by Lighthouse's agentic audits. It is unrelated to WebMCP's browser API.
sec_convention_llms_txt_present_why.description: Security finding convention-llms-txt-present: why it matters.

sec_convention_manifest_invalid_fix.message: Serve valid JSON or remove the file.
sec_convention_manifest_invalid_fix.description: Security finding convention-manifest-invalid: what to do.

sec_convention_manifest_invalid_title.message: A /.well-known/webmcp file is served but is not JSON

sec_convention_manifest_invalid_why.message: The path answers but its body does not parse as JSON; a reader expecting the convention gets nothing usable.
sec_convention_manifest_invalid_why.description: Security finding convention-manifest-invalid: why it matters.

sec_convention_manifest_present_fix.message: Keep it consistent with the tools the page actually registers, or remove it; it is not a standard.
sec_convention_manifest_present_fix.description: Security finding convention-manifest-present: what to do.

sec_convention_manifest_present_why.message: A discovery manifest in the community convention was found. It is not part of the W3C CG draft; some auditors and directories read it. Agents using the browser API do not need it.
sec_convention_manifest_present_why.description: Security finding convention-manifest-present: why it matters.

sec_convention_permissions_policy_absent.message: Send Permissions-Policy: tools=() on pages that do not use WebMCP; otherwise nothing to do.
sec_convention_permissions_policy_absent.description: Security finding convention-permissions-policy-absent: what to do.

sec_convention_permissions_policy_absent.message: No Permissions-Policy for tools on the page response

Without the header the default applies: WebMCP is allowed for the page and same-origin frames. A page that does not use WebMCP can send Permissions-Policy: tools=() so no injected script can register tools (spec §6.4.1).
sec_convention_permissions_policy_absent.description: Security finding convention-permissions-policy-absent: why it matters.

sec_convention_permissions_policy_fix.message: Check that the allowlist matches your intent.
sec_convention_permissions_policy_fix.description: Security finding convention-permissions-policy: what to do.

sec_convention_permissions_policy_title.message: The page's Permissions-Policy names the tools feature

sec_convention_permissions_policy_why.message: The response header restricts or delegates WebMCP explicitly (spec §6.4.1). This is the mechanism the specification recommends to disable WebMCP where it is not used.
sec_convention_permissions_policy_why.description: Security finding convention-permissions-policy: why it matters.

sec_cross_origin_frame_tools_fix.message: Confirm the embed is intended; grant Explorer access to the frame's origin to review its tools.
sec_cross_origin_frame_tools_fix.description: Security finding cross-origin-frame-tools: what to do.

sec_cross_origin_frame_tools_title.message: Tools from a frame of another origin

sec_cross_origin_frame_tools_why.message: A frame of another origin exposes tools on this page. Agents see them next to yours.
sec_cross_origin_frame_tools_why.description: Security finding cross-origin-frame-tools: why it matters.

sec_debugging_tool_exposed_fix.message: Register debugging tools only in development builds or behind a developer setting.
sec_debugging_tool_exposed_fix.description: Security finding debugging-tool-exposed: what to do.

sec_debugging_tool_exposed_title.message: A debugging tool is exposed on this page

sec_debugging_tool_exposed_why.message: annotations.debugging marks a tool for developer tooling. On a page people visit it is callable by any agent.
sec_debugging_tool_exposed_why.description: Security finding debugging-tool-exposed: why it matters.

sec_delegated_tools_policy_fix.message: Keep allow="tools" only on embeds you trust to act for your visitors.
sec_delegated_tools_policy_fix.description: Security finding delegated-tools-policy: what to do.

sec_delegated_tools_policy_title.message: The page delegates the tools policy to another origin

sec_delegated_tools_policy_why.message: An iframe carries allow="tools": the embedded origin may register tools on this page (spec §6.4.1 describes the policy; Chrome recommends exposing only to trusted origins).
sec_delegated_tools_policy_why.description: Security finding delegated-tools-policy: why it matters.

sec_high_risk_read_without_hint_fix.message: Consider consequentialHint on reads that disclose sensitive data, and minimise what the tool returns.
sec_high_risk_read_without_hint_fix.description: Security finding high-risk-read-without-hint: what to do.

sec_high_risk_read_without_hint_title.message: A read of sensitive data without consequentialHint

sec_high_risk_read_without_hint_why.message: The tool reads addresses, balances, credentials or health data. Whether read-only disclosure should require confirmation is an open specification discussion (#331); until it settles, declaring the hint is the conservative choice.
sec_high_risk_read_without_hint_why.description: Security finding high-risk-read-without-hint: why it matters.

sec_legacy_host_fix.description: Security finding legacy-host: what to do.

sec_legacy_host_title.message: The legacy navigator.modelContext host is in use

sec_legacy_host_why.message: The API moved to document.modelContext; a page relying on the navigator alias depends on a compatibility path.
sec_legacy_host_why.description: Security finding legacy-host: why it matters.

sec_no_tools_policy_open_fix.message: Send Permissions-Policy: tools=() from pages that do not use WebMCP.
sec_no_tools_policy_open_fix.description: Security finding no-tools-policy-open: what to do.

sec_no_tools_policy_open_title.message: No tools, but WebMCP stays open on this page

sec_no_tools_policy_open_why.message: A page that exposes no tools can still receive tools from any injected script. Permissions-Policy: tools=() closes the API for the document and its frames before scripts run (spec §6.4.1).
sec_no_tools_policy_open_why.description: Security finding no-tools-policy-open: why it matters.

sec_opaque_origin_tool_fix.message: Give the frame a real origin or remove its tools.
sec_opaque_origin_tool_fix.description: Security finding opaque-origin-tool: what to do.

sec_opaque_origin_tool_title.message: A tool from an opaque origin

sec_opaque_origin_tool_why.message: Sandboxed or about:blank frames have an opaque origin; their tools cannot be attributed to a site.
sec_opaque_origin_tool_why.description: Security finding opaque-origin-tool: why it matters.

sec_output_directive_fix.message: Return data, not prose aimed at the agent; mark results that carry other people's text with untrustedContentHint.
sec_output_directive_fix.description: Security finding output-directive: what to do.

sec_output_directive_title.message: The result reads like an instruction to the agent

sec_output_directive_why.message: The tool's output contains phrases addressed to the agent. Output injection (spec §6.3.1.2) is how a page or its users steer an agent after the call.
sec_output_directive_why.description: Security finding output-directive: why it matters.

sec_output_markup_fix.message: Return plain data; let the agent format it.
sec_output_markup_fix.description: Security finding output-markup: what to do.

sec_output_markup_title.message: Markup or template tokens in the result

sec_output_markup_why.message: HTML tags, code fences or prompt-template tokens in a result are a carrier for injected instructions.
sec_output_markup_why.description: Security finding output-markup: why it matters.

sec_output_over_budget_fix.message: Return less, page the result, or return a reference the agent can follow.
sec_output_over_budget_fix.description: Security finding output-over-budget: what to do.

sec_output_over_budget_title.message: The result exceeds the 1.5K output budget

sec_output_over_budget_why.message: Chrome's guidance budgets a tool output at about 1,500 characters; larger results cost context and widen the surface for output injection.
sec_output_over_budget_why.description: Security finding output-over-budget: why it matters.

sec_output_personal_data_fix.message: Return only what the task needs; mark results carrying personal or user-written data with untrustedContentHint.
sec_output_personal_data_fix.description: Security finding output-personal-data: what to do.

sec_output_personal_data_title.message: The result appears to contain personal data

sec_output_personal_data_why.message: An e-mail address, a phone number or a card-like number came back from a valid call without untrustedContentHint. The result travels to whichever agent called the tool (spec §6.3.3, OWASP MCP10).
sec_output_personal_data_why.description: Security finding output-personal-data: why it matters.

sec_probe_call_failed_fix.message: Make the example that the schema implies work, or tighten the schema (enum, format, examples).
sec_probe_call_failed_fix.description: Security finding probe-call-failed: what to do.

sec_probe_call_failed_title.message: The tool failed on generated valid arguments

sec_probe_call_failed_why.message: Called with arguments generated from its own schema (required fields and defaults), the tool returned an error. An agent would meet the same error on its first call.
sec_probe_call_failed_why.description: Security finding probe-call-failed: why it matters.

sec_re_registered_in_session_fix.message: Compare a snapshot taken before with the current contract (Tools → Snapshots); register tools once per document where possible.
sec_re_registered_in_session_fix.description: Security finding re-registered-in-session: what to do.

sec_re_registered_in_session_title.message: Removed and registered again in this session

sec_re_registered_in_session_why.message: A tool that disappears and comes back may be the same tool re-mounted, or a different contract under the same name (arXiv 2606.06387, spec issue #92). The timeline saw the change; Explorer did not compare the contracts.
sec_re_registered_in_session_why.description: Security finding re-registered-in-session: why it matters.

sec_readonly_claim_on_mutating_verb_fix.message: Remove readOnlyHint or rename the tool so the name matches what it does; re-review hints after each change.
sec_readonly_claim_on_mutating_verb_fix.description: Security finding readonly-claim-on-mutating-verb: what to do.

sec_readonly_claim_on_mutating_verb_titl.message: readOnlyHint on a tool whose name says it changes state

sec_readonly_claim_on_mutating_verb_why.message: Agents may skip confirmation for read-only tools. A read-only label on a verb such as delete, pay or update is either stale or wrong, and the spec says declared intent cannot be verified (§6.3.2).
sec_readonly_claim_on_mutating_verb_why.description: Security finding readonly-claim-on-mutating-verb: why it matters.

sec_registered_more_than_once_fix.message: Register once per document, or unregister explicitly with the AbortSignal before registering again.
sec_registered_more_than_once_fix.description: Security finding registered-more-than-once: what to do.

sec_registered_more_than_once_title.message: Several registerTool() calls for this name

sec_registered_more_than_once_why.message: Instrumentation Mode saw more than one registration call for this tool in this document. Repeated registration is the mechanism a replacement attack uses; it is also what a component that re-renders does.
sec_registered_more_than_once_why.description: Security finding registered-more-than-once: why it matters.

sec_sensitive_parameter_fix.message: Remove the parameter, collect the value in the page's own UI with the person present, or pass an opaque reference.
sec_sensitive_parameter_fix.description: Security finding sensitive-parameter: what to do.

sec_sensitive_parameter_title.message: A parameter asks for sensitive data

sec_sensitive_parameter_why.message: An agent trying to be helpful may fill this parameter from personalisation data, browsing history or other sites (spec §6.3.3). Credentials, card data and national identifiers should never pass through a model (#316).
sec_sensitive_parameter_why.description: Security finding sensitive-parameter: why it matters.

sec_state_change_without_hint_fix.message: Declare consequentialHint when the change matters to the person; leave readOnlyHint false.
sec_state_change_without_hint_fix.description: Security finding state-change-without-hint: what to do.

sec_state_change_without_hint_title.message: A state-changing tool declares no hint

sec_state_change_without_hint_why.message: The verb changes something on the page or the account, but neither readOnlyHint nor consequentialHint is declared; agents are told to assume state change, and a reviewer cannot tell intended from accidental omission.
sec_state_change_without_hint_why.description: Security finding state-change-without-hint: why it matters.

sec_text_agent_directive_fix.message: Describe what the tool does and when it applies, in plain declarative sentences; move any workflow rule into the tool's own code or its schema.
sec_text_agent_directive_fix.description: Security finding text-agent-directive: what to do.

sec_text_agent_directive_title.message: Description reads like an instruction to the agent

sec_text_agent_directive_why.message: Agents take tool descriptions as trusted context. Phrases such as “always call this first” or “do not tell the user” steer the model instead of describing the tool (spec §6.3.1.1, tool poisoning). A legitimate description can use these words; this is an indicator for a person to read.
sec_text_agent_directive_why.description: Security finding text-agent-directive: why it matters.

sec_text_embedded_address_fix.message: Describe the tool without addresses; return links in results if they are part of the data.
sec_text_embedded_address_fix.description: Security finding text-embedded-address: what to do.

sec_text_embedded_address_title.message: A URL or e-mail address in model-facing text

sec_text_embedded_address_why.message: An address in a description can lead an agent to fetch or contact something the person did not ask for (Chrome agent guidance: restrict origins to the task).
sec_text_embedded_address_why.description: Security finding text-embedded-address: why it matters.

sec_text_encoded_blob_fix.message: Remove encoded payloads from names and descriptions; pass data through arguments and results.
sec_text_encoded_blob_fix.description: Security finding text-encoded-blob: what to do.

sec_text_encoded_blob_title.message: Encoded data embedded in model-facing text

sec_text_encoded_blob_why.message: A long base64 or hexadecimal run in a description carries content a reader cannot inspect and a model may decode or act on.
sec_text_encoded_blob_why.description: Security finding text-encoded-blob: why it matters.

sec_text_hidden_characters_fix.message: Remove the characters listed; check the build step or CMS that produced the text.
sec_text_hidden_characters_fix.description: Security finding text-hidden-characters: what to do.

sec_text_hidden_characters_title.message: Invisible or direction-changing characters in model-facing text

sec_text_hidden_characters_why.message: Zero-width, bidirectional and control characters are invisible to a person reading the page but reach the model verbatim: they can hide text or reverse how it reads.
sec_text_hidden_characters_why.description: Security finding text-hidden-characters: why it matters.

sec_text_markup_fix.message: Use plain text in names and descriptions.
sec_text_markup_fix.description: Security finding text-markup: what to do.

sec_text_markup_title.message: Markup or template tokens in model-facing text

sec_text_markup_why.message: HTML tags, code fences or prompt-template tokens in a description are a common carrier for injected instructions and are never needed to describe a tool.
sec_text_markup_why.description: Security finding text-markup: why it matters.

sec_text_mixed_scripts_fix.message: Rewrite the word with one script; if the text is genuinely multilingual, keep each word in a single script.
sec_text_mixed_scripts_fix.description: Security finding text-mixed-scripts: what to do.

sec_text_mixed_scripts_title.message: A word mixes Latin letters with Cyrillic or Greek look-alikes

sec_text_mixed_scripts_why.message: Look-alike letters make two different strings read the same to a person while a model and a validator see two different words (Unicode TR36).
sec_text_mixed_scripts_why.description: Security finding text-mixed-scripts: why it matters.

sec_text_over_budget_fix.message: Shorten to the budgets; put details in the schema's parameter descriptions.
sec_text_over_budget_fix.description: Security finding text-over-budget: what to do.

sec_text_over_budget_title.message: Text beyond the budgets agents apply

sec_text_over_budget_why.message: Chrome's guidance budgets a description at 500 characters, a parameter description at 150 and a name at 30; longer text is more likely to be truncated or to hide an instruction in padding (spec §6.4.2).
sec_text_over_budget_why.description: Security finding text-over-budget: why it matters.

sec_third_party_registration_fix.message: Review the script, pin its version or serve it from your origin; log registrations in production.
sec_third_party_registration_fix.description: Security finding third-party-registration: what to do.

sec_third_party_registration_title.message: Registered by a script from another origin

sec_third_party_registration_why.message: This tool was registered by code served from a different origin than the page: a CDN, an edge bridge or a plugin. Any script on the page can add or replace tools (mid-session tool injection, arXiv 2606.06387).
sec_third_party_registration_why.description: Security finding third-party-registration: why it matters.

sec_ugc_without_untrusted_hint_fix.message: Set annotations.untrustedContentHint to true on tools that return text written by others.
sec_ugc_without_untrusted_hint_fix.description: Security finding ugc-without-untrusted-hint: what to do.

sec_ugc_without_untrusted_hint_title.message: Content from other people without untrustedContentHint

sec_ugc_without_untrusted_hint_why.message: Reviews, comments, messages or fetched page text can carry instructions aimed at the agent (output injection, spec §6.3.1.2). untrustedContentHint tells agents to treat the result as data.
sec_ugc_without_untrusted_hint_why.description: Security finding ugc-without-untrusted-hint: why it matters.

sec_unbounded_string_fix.message: Add maxLength, an enum or a format where the value has one; validate in the tool's code regardless.
sec_unbounded_string_fix.description: Security finding unbounded-string: what to do.

sec_unbounded_string_title.message: Free-text parameters without a length bound

sec_unbounded_string_why.message: Unbounded strings widen what an injected instruction can carry (spec §6.4.2). Chrome advises validating strictly in code; a maxLength or an enum in the schema also tells agents what fits.
sec_unbounded_string_why.description: Security finding unbounded-string: why it matters.

sec_text_active_payload_title.message: Active payload marker in tool text

sec_text_active_payload_why.message: Script tags, instruction overrides or external Markdown images may redirect an agent. This is an indicator, not proof of execution or exfiltration.

sec_text_active_payload_fix.message: Replace agent instructions with a factual action description. Review every schema description; keep untrusted text out of trusted instructions.

sec_mutation_hints_incomplete_title.message: Mutating intent is not fully declared

sec_mutation_hints_incomplete_why.message: The action verb suggests a state change. WebMCP hints are advisory and cannot enforce approval or authorization.

sec_mutation_hints_incomplete_fix.message: For the reviewed mutation set readOnlyHint:false and consequentialHint:true. Implement confirmation and server authorization separately.

sec_permissive_object_why.message: Additional properties are explicitly allowed, or the sensitive tool has no closed object boundary. This describes the schema, not server validation.

sec_permissive_object_fix.message: Review additionalProperties:false and nested constraints. Check composed schemas and compatibility before closing objects; validate again on the server.

sec_mutating_auto_submit_why.message: toolautosubmit removes the native manual-submit step. Authentication and custom confirmation handlers remain unknown. agentInvoked identifies provenance, not human consent.

sec_mutating_auto_submit_fix.message: Review removing toolautosubmit for sensitive actions. Bind authorization and approval to the exact account, arguments and operation on the server.

sec_legacy_registration_why.message: This observed registration uses the navigator namespace or provideContext. Compatibility depends on the runtime; presence alone is not an exploit.

sec_legacy_registration_fix.message: Migrate to document.modelContext.registerTool with AbortSignal cleanup after qualifying the target browser. Do not register a duplicate callback.

sec_token_estimate_over_budget_why.message: The estimate exceeds 800 tokens, using UTF-8 bytes divided by four and rounded up. Exact token counts depend on the model tokenizer.

sec_token_estimate_over_budget_fix.message: Shorten the action description and parameter descriptions without removing necessary constraints. Measure with the intended model tokenizer if an exact budget is required.

sec_ambiguous_description_why.message: Different tool names have a word-set Jaccard similarity of at least 0.80. Lexical overlap does not prove identical behaviour.

sec_ambiguous_description_fix.message: Describe each action’s unique scope, inputs and result. Avoid instructions telling the agent to prefer one tool or to call another first.

sec_convention_csp_why.message: This records a credential-free response header, not the effective policy. A missing header does not rule out a meta policy.

sec_convention_csp_fix.message: Review CSP against the real scripts and connections; stage changes with Report-Only and application tests.

sec_convention_cors_why.message: Header evidence only; no browser cross-origin request was tested. Wildcard origin with credentials is incompatible with credentialed CORS, not proof of a credential leak.

sec_convention_cors_fix.message: Allow only intended origins where needed. Do not enable wildcard CORS to silence a diagnostic; test authenticated behaviour separately.

sec_convention_unavailable_why.message: The response failed, redirected, exceeded the size cap or returned a non-success status. Optional discovery files are not mandatory WebMCP endpoints.

sec_convention_unavailable_fix.message: Inspect the listed response if you intended to publish this convention. Absence alone requires no security fix; no automatic retry was made.
